summary: A GPL-3.0-only research archive (Nested Resonance Memory / DUALITY-ZERO) whose shipped, user-facing surfaces are the AV Field Toolkit — 56 phone-first tool pages listed across nine trade registries on one shared runtime, where a trade is a config and never a fork — and Collage Studio, a browser generative-collage tool.
_note: Scope, amended 2026-08-19: this is the REPO'S manifest, served at the site root. The two surfaces the Wish It Better network lists by url — the AV Field Toolkit at /av/ and Collage Studio at /collage/ — each publish their OWN manifest beside the page a card opens (tracked at av/wish-it-better.json and tools/collage-studio/public/wish-it-better.json), because origin (criterion 5) is a property of each surface and not of the repo: the two have different lineages, and one file copied to both urls could carry only one — which is what this file did from 2026-08-13 to 2026-08-19, and what the network sweep in mrdirno/vibe-cards reported as unclosable. Level, licence and the wish queue are still properties of the repo — one LICENSE, one wish queue (av_tool_requests, whose trade column already carries both the eight trades and Collage Studio), one CI workflow, one Pages artifact — so the per-surface files declare the same L0 and GPL-3.0-only. The eight trades are configs on one runtime, not eight projects; the network addresses each surface by url instead. Level is L0, not L1, on two counts checked at the artifact: (1) the evals that ask whether a phone can actually reach a control — the seven harnesses in tools/toolkit-gates/ — appear zero times in .github/workflows/deploy_bridge.yml, so 'every shipped change carries an eval' is false, though that workflow's own 38 fail-the-build assertions do run against the built artifact on every deploy; (2) av_wishing_well.py gates new -> building -> shipped|declined and never deletes a row, but it has no expiry, so the K-cycle auto-expiry in WISH_IT_BETTER.md §2 is unimplemented and terminal states are reached only by hand. Two things a forker should know about the channel: nothing notifies the wisher although the form promises it — the queue's only consumer sends no mail — and the well's URL and key are injected from repo secrets at deploy time, so a fork gets the placeholder, the runtime detects it, and the well refuses to send until you wire your own backend.
